name: Confidence Penalty
tagline: Cross-entropy minus a softmax-entropy bonus, which discourages overconfident outputs and reduces MIA leakage.
diff_from_baseline: Pereyra et al., ICLR 2017 workshop (Regularizing Neural Networks by Penalizing Confident Output Distributions). Standard MIA-defense baseline that adds negative softmax entropy to CE; reduces confidence gap between members and non-members.

name: ERM (vanilla CE)
tagline: Standard cross-entropy training with no defense; the unprotected baseline that exposes the maximum membership-inference leakage.
diff_from_baseline: Empirical risk minimization with cross-entropy; the no-defense baseline against which all MIA-defense methods are compared.

name: Label Smoothing
tagline: Replaces one-hot targets with (1 - eps) one-hot + eps/C, lowering output confidence and reducing membership-inference signal.
diff_from_baseline: Szegedy et al., CVPR 2016 (Rethinking the Inception Architecture). Standard MIA-defense baseline: soft targets reduce overconfidence on training points and shrink the confidence gap exploited by MIAs.

name: RelaxLoss
tagline: Two-phase alternation: even epochs drive batch CE toward target alpha; odd epochs do CE descent or posterior flattening on already-correct samples.
pseudocode:
1. Per dataset choose $\alpha = 0.5$ if $C=100$ else $1.0$ (config-tied target loss level)
2. Compute $L_{\text{ce}} = \overline{\mathrm{CE}(z, y)}$ and per-sample $\ell_i$
3. Even epoch: return $|L_{\text{ce}} - \alpha|$ (gradient toward target, ascent if below)
4. Odd epoch and $L_{\text{ce}} > \alpha$: standard CE descent
5. Odd epoch and $L_{\text{ce}} \le \alpha$: build flattened soft targets with $p_t = \mathrm{clip}(\mathrm{softmax}(z)_y, \le 1)$ on true class, $(1-p_t)/(C-1)$ elsewhere (detached)
6. Return $\frac{1}{N}\sum_i \big[(1 - \mathbb{1}[\hat{y}_i = y_i])\cdot \mathrm{CE}_{\text{soft}, i} - \ell_i\big]$ (sign-flipped CE on correct samples + soft CE on wrong)
diff_from_baseline: Chen et al., ICLR 2022 (RelaxLoss: Defending Membership Inference Attacks without Losing Utility). Faithful port of the official source/cifar/defense/relaxloss.py - bidirectional gradient toward a target loss level plus posterior flattening on correctly classified samples.
